column1: # Command codes on /Q_ServCmdRcver -- Barracuda -> /tuxedo, the WRITE path.
# The 404-byte command is built in a global buffer at Barracuda 0x55d8d0 and
# sent with mq_send(mqd from the global at 0x55ae68, buf, 404, prio=1). The code
# lives at buf+0x04; +0x08 and +0x0C are command-specific parameters, NOT fixed
# fields (for command 6285 they are the x/y of a simulated touch).
# Regenerate with:  python dispatch_tree.py <rootfs>/tuxedo
# It walks CReceiverThread::run @0x147158 carrying an interval and an exclusion
# set for the received code, narrowing both on every conditional branch, and
# reads each handler as belonging to whatever the constraints still permit.
# 774 words, 0 undecodable, no path left unresolved. Handler names are the
# binary's own Qt symbols, so the semantics are the vendor's.
# FOUR EARLIER ATTEMPTS AT THIS TABLE WERE WRONG, each looking complete:
#  * cmp + beq gave 40 codes and missed every cmp/bne form.
#  * cmp + the branch at cmp+4 gave 56 and missed 112, whose beq sits five
#    words after its cmp with unrelated stores in between.
#  * treating cmp/bhs as a search pivot rather than a case gave 55 and lost
#    300-303, which really do share one handler. 300 was published from a
#    pivot, withdrawn as a false positive, and is back -- as a range.
#  * 126 and 128 have no comparison of their own at all: after cmp #127 and
#    cmp #125 the only value that can still fall through is 126, so gcc emits
#    the handler with no test. No pattern over instruction pairs can see that.
# Anything that claims fewer than 84 has lost some.
# Not every case does work. 100 and 116 print their own vendor name and
# return. 102 and 123-124 branch straight back to the receive loop: accepted
# and silently discarded. Anything with no case reaches the default arm at
# 0x14723c, which prints "Web:ERR:Wrong Command from Web" and drains the next
# message.
# The sender column is what Barracuda is known to send (sender_args.py). A "-"
# does not mean unreachable: setarmwithcode, setdisarmwithcode,
# setOccupancyMode and setPartitionArmed take the code as an argument and
# those call sites are not resolved yet.
# code<TAB>handler_va<TAB>handler<TAB>barracuda_sender
